newsitem.title: USA: Dole says character will count, seeks Perot voters.
newsitem.headline: Dole says character will count, seeks Perot voters.

text.p: Republican presidential candidate Bob Dole, vowing to pick up the campaign pace after a break on Sunday in his marathon, renewed his attack on White House ethics and asked Ross Perot's supporters for their votes.

Addressing a rally of some 4,000 supporters in this city east of Los Angeles, Dole said Americans would show character mattered in the election, and said the administration of President Bill Clinton administration was bent on retaining power however it could.
"I really believe the election will determine, does character count?" he said. "And if the American people say it does not, I will be surprised."
"We are going to prevail because the American people have had enough," he said. "They've had enough and they're going to make a change," he said.
Referring to ethical questions surrounding the Clinton administration, Dole said, "What a mess ... there is nothing they will not do to keep power."
Supporters of Reform Party candidate Ross Perot should vote for Dole out of a shared aim of defeating Clinton, he said.

"We're seeing in many states ... the Perot vote will make a difference, and Perot doesn't want Bill Clinton elected, I know that for certain," Dole said. "So if you're a Perot supporter and you want to defeat Bill Clinton, what do you do? You vote for Bob Dole and Jack Kemp."
Dole was joined at the rally, which was lit by a glowing late afternoon sun, his wife, Elizabeth, his running mate, Kemp, actress Bo Derek and California Gov. Pete Wilson.

The final weekend of the campaign was billed as a "non- stop" 96-hour marathon across the country. But Dole managed to work in a six-hour break on Sunday in the California beach community of La Jolla to nap and clean up.

Dole's press secretary Nelson Warfield called the hotel stop "basically a hygiene break. In the middle of his heroic national marathon, Bob Dole took a break to clean up with a shower and a shave," he said. "As filthy as Bill Clinton's campaign has been, he might as well consider cleaning up too."
But Dole set out to resume the hectic schedule. "We're going to pick up the pace," he said before going to the Loma Linda rally.
As he spoke here, Dole's voice showed signs of strain. He had told reporters earlier he had slept for about four hours during the break and said he was taking cough drops for a throat irritation.
Dole was to continue campaigning in California through a midnight stop in Sacramento, then head for Arizona, New Mexico, Texas, Louisiana, Tennessee and Iowa on Monday.
Dole intended to finish his campaign Tuesday in Independence, Missouri, the hometown of Harry Truman, who came from behind to win the 1948 presidential race.
He will then cast his vote in his hometown of Russell, Kansas.
Dole hoped his grueling campaign push would help him narrow a persistent poll deficit against Clinton and carry him to victory.
In California, with 54 of the 270 electoral votes needed to win the presidency, Dole continued to trail Clinton in the polls.
An internal campaign poll finished on Saturday showed Dole trailed Clinton by 4 percentage points in the state, Dole California adviser Ken Khachigian said.
The poll of likely voters among a group of 400 registered voters surveyed had a five-point margin of error.
It remained to be seen whether Dole could close the gap, but state Republicans were likely to at least hold their own in congressional races, Khachigian said.
